key_insight: Light-MER shows that multimodal emotion recognition can reach state-of-the-art performance with a sub-1B model by distilling knowledge from a much larger teacher instead of relying on 7B+ parameters.
engineering_relevance: This makes multimodal emotion models more practical for real-time deployment on robots, mobile devices, and other resource-constrained systems by reducing compute and latency.
method: Knowledge distillation from a large teacher to a lightweight student model
Optimal-transport-based transfer using Sliced Wasserstein Distance plus hidden-state alignment
GRPO-style multi-reward optimization to balance recognition quality and efficiency
evidence_signal: The abstract reports extensive experiments on nine benchmark datasets, where Light-MER achieves state-of-the-art performance while improving inference efficiency.
watch_item: Results depend on effective teacher quality and distillation training stability, so the method may require careful tuning to avoid efficiency gains hurting recognition performance.
paper_title: Do We Really Need Multimodal Emotion Language Models Larger Than 1B Parameters?
